subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw's core read tool add a narrow safe fallback for known binary document formats, or should document handling remain only in dedicated document/PDF tools and tool guidance?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the current token-waste path, but the durable product choice is whether read should fail helpfully for binary documents or grow inline parsing behavior.

options.title: Add narrow read fallback
options.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable message for known binary Office/PDF formats and leaves parsing to dedicated tools.

options.title: Limit this to tool guidance
options.body: Keep read as a text/image tool and update descriptions/docs to steer agents toward pdf or document tools, accepting that unsupported binary reads can still happen.

options.title: Fold into broader document ingestion
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader provider-native file/document and attachment extraction work, with security and dependency review before implementation.

recommendation.title: Add narrow read fallback
recommendation.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable message for known binary Office/PDF formats and leaves parsing to dedicated tools.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current-main history signal on the read tool and wrapper path that would need the safe fallback.
